narrative.overview:
This system is a demonstration before it is a presentation. Every layout decision is a proof of design competence: the grid holds because the designer understands grids, the type hierarchy is exact because the designer understands hierarchy, the restraint is deliberate because the designer understands ornament.

The palette is near-monochromatic. Warm ink grounds everything; the single orange accent activates sparingly; every neutral carries a warm tilt that makes the near-black feel considered rather than default-digital. Screen-blue grays are prohibited.

Nothing competes with the work. Navigation disappears. Every component steps back to let portfolio pieces occupy the frame. If an element cannot justify its presence, it is absent.
keyCharacteristics: Warm-tinted neutrals throughout; never screen-blue or charcoal-gray
Single Precision Signal (orange) on ≤10% of any surface
Geometric sans + technical mono; two faces, no exceptions
Flat surfaces at rest; depth only for structural separation
Motion for state acknowledgement only; never choreography or decoration

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: The Precision Signal appears on ≤10% of any surface. It marks active state, focus, and brand identity. It does not fill backgrounds, decorate cards, or announce sections. Its rarity is the point.

rules.name: The Warm Ground Rule
rules.body: Every neutral leans warm (OKLCH hue 45–60). The cool-blue grays in the existing codebase are prohibited in new work. When in doubt, shift warmer.

rules.name: The Swiss Type Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is built through scale and weight alone. Color is never used to signal importance in text.

rules.name: The Mono Reserve Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono is restricted to labels, timestamps, buttons, and UI controls. It does not appear in prose headings or article body text.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: No shadow at rest. Brightness-shift on hover. shadow-layer only for structural image and device mockup separation.

dos: Do use Warm Ink (oklch(9% 0.007 50)) for all near-black values. The warm ground is non-negotiable.
Do keep the Precision Signal to ≤10% of any surface.
Do build type hierarchy through scale and weight alone.
Do use filter: brightness() for hover states on interactive containers.
Do restrict IBM Plex Mono to labels, timestamps, and UI controls.
Do apply text-wrap: balance to all headings.
Do use the two-layer card structure before reaching for borders or shadows.
Do use ease-out curves (ease-out-quart or expo) for all transitions.
donts: Don't animate anything for decoration. State transitions only.
Don't use scroll-triggered reveal animations or parallax.
Don't use the .mesh grain texture on content areas or over portfolio work.
Don't use glassmorphism, 3D blobs, aurora backgrounds, or gradient-heavy treatments.
Don't fill large surfaces with the brand orange.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with gradient fill).
Don't use side-stripe borders (border-left > 1px as a colored accent).
Don't apply shadow-layer to cards, navigation, tooltips, or dropdowns.
Don't replicate generic creative agency patterns: rotating hero text, identical icon-heading-text card grids, footer rows of social links.
Don't use cool-blue-gray neutrals (#0d0e12, #13141b). Replace with warm-tinted values.
